verdict: Fifth Third's first year with Comerica shows in the numbers: net interest income rose 49%, and even after $211M of after-tax merger and other items, the bank earned $828M for common shareholders.

segments.name: Net interest income
segments.note: Interest earned on loans and securities minus interest paid on deposits and borrowings — up 49%, mostly because Comerica's balance sheet was added.

segments.name: Noninterest income
segments.note: Fees and other non-interest revenue: wealth and asset management ($259M), commercial payments ($256M), consumer banking ($158M), capital markets ($147M) and more.

opex.name: Compensation & benefits
opex.note: Pay and benefits — the bank's biggest cost, up 43% on the larger combined workforce.

opex.name: Technology & communications
opex.note: Technology and communications, up sharply as the two banks' systems were combined.

opex.name: Occupancy, equipment & other
opex.note: Branches and occupancy ($144M), card and processing ($60M), equipment ($59M), loan and lease costs ($47M), plus $400M of other expense — which includes merger-related charges.

footerNote: Bank layout (the same one our JPMorgan pages use): revenue is net interest income plus fee and other noninterest income, and the 'direct cost' is the provision for credit losses — money set aside for loans that may not be repaid. Net income was $866M; after $38M of preferred dividends, $828M was available to common shareholders.

takeaways.title: Comerica made the bank much bigger
takeaways.text: Average loans were $179B versus $123B a year ago and average deposits $238B versus $165B. The systems conversion finished this quarter with, the bank says, strong client and banker retention.

takeaways.title: Adjusted EPS vs $0.90 reported
takeaways.text: Reported EPS of $0.90 includes $0.23 of certain items — mainly Comerica merger charges. Excluding them, EPS was $1.13 and adjusted return on tangible common equity was 20.6%.

takeaways.title: Credit stayed calm
takeaways.text: Net charge-offs were just 0.31% of loans and the provision for credit losses fell 38% year over year to $122M — credit quality held up through the merger integration.

oneTimers: Certain items cut EPS by $0.23 (after tax $211M): merger-related charges ($171M after tax; $215M pre-tax in expenses and $10M against revenue), interchange litigation matters ($26M) and technology-related asset impairments ($14M).
Year-over-year comparisons span the Comerica acquisition, which closed earlier in 2026 — most growth rates reflect the bigger combined bank, not organic growth.
